metadata.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli for direct production of 1,4-butanediol

reference.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli for direct production of 1,4-butanediol

engineering_problem.problem_statement: E. coli cannot naturally produce 1,4-butanediol (1,4-BDO); no native biosynthetic pathway to this product exists in the host.
trigger_conditions: target product has no native biosynthetic pathway in the host organism
engineering objective requires introducing a heterologous or fully synthetic pathway

observations: the host has no endogenous enzymatic route from central metabolism to 1,4-butanediol
introducing enzyme activity alone, without host-level support, may not be sufficient for efficient production
bottlenecks: absence of a native 1,4-BDO biosynthetic pathway
precursor and cofactor availability for a newly introduced heterologous pathway
metabolic burden of expressing a multi-step heterologous pathway
biological_diagnosis.mechanistic_explanation: Because no native pathway to 1,4-BDO exists, production requires constructing a complete heterologous (or synthetic) enzymatic route and integrating it with host metabolism; simply inserting the pathway genes is insufficient if the host cannot supply adequate precursor and cofactor flux to support it.

engineering_hypothesis.hypothesis: Combining de novo pathway construction with host-background optimization for precursor and cofactor supply enables functional 1,4-BDO production in a host that lacks the native pathway.
engineering_hypothesis.expected_effect: acquisition of a functional biosynthetic route to 1,4-BDO, with host optimization improving achievable flux beyond pathway insertion alone

engineering_actions.gene_or_pathway: multi-gene heterologous pathway; specific gene identities are not specified in the problem summary available to this V1 knowledge base and require review of the primary text
engineering_actions.source: Yim H. et al., 2011, Nature Chemical Biology, DOI:10.1038/nchembio.580
engineering_actions.rationale: since the host lacks a native pathway to the product, constructing and inserting a synthetic/heterologous pathway is the primary engineering action rather than modifying an existing pathway.
engineering_actions.expected_effect: establishes baseline biosynthetic capability for 1,4-BDO in the host
engineering_actions.risk: heterologous enzymes may have suboptimal kinetics or expression in E. coli; a multi-step pathway adds metabolic burden that can reduce growth
validation: confirm 1,4-BDO production analytically (e.g. HPLC or GC-MS)
assess strain growth and viability with the pathway expressed

engineering_actions.target: precursor and cofactor supply for the heterologous pathway
engineering_actions.gene_or_pathway: host central metabolism and cofactor-regeneration systems; specific gene identities are not specified in the problem summary available to this V1 knowledge base
engineering_actions.source: Yim H. et al., 2011, Nature Chemical Biology, DOI:10.1038/nchembio.580
engineering_actions.rationale: pathway insertion alone is often insufficient without addressing precursor and cofactor (e.g. redox cofactor) requirements from host metabolism.
engineering_actions.expected_effect: improved precursor/cofactor balance supporting higher heterologous pathway throughput
engineering_actions.risk: cofactor-supply engineering can perturb central metabolism and unrelated host pathways
validation: measure relevant cofactor pool ratios before and after host optimization
compare 1,4-BDO titer with and without host-background optimization

decision_rules.condition: host organism lacks a native biosynthetic pathway for the target product
decision_rules.recommended_strategy: construct a synthetic/heterologous pathway rather than attempting to redirect a nonexistent native route
decision_rules.reason: there is no endogenous pathway to modify or redirect flux through

decision_rules.condition: a heterologous pathway has been introduced
decision_rules.recommended_strategy: combine pathway insertion with host-background optimization
decision_rules.reason: pathway insertion alone is frequently insufficient without addressing precursor/cofactor supply in the host

decision_rules.condition: designing a de novo biosynthetic pathway
decision_rules.recommended_strategy: explicitly evaluate precursor and cofactor requirements during pathway and strain design
decision_rules.reason: mismatched precursor or cofactor availability limits achievable flux regardless of enzyme selection

generalizable_rules: when a host lacks a native pathway to a target product, prioritize pathway construction over pathway modification
de novo pathway engineering should be paired with host-level optimization of precursor and cofactor supply, not treated as a standalone gene-insertion task
